title: Definition
body_md: The $S$-fence, denoted by $\phi_{n}$, is a fence-like poset, with element $\{x_1,\ldots, x_n\}$ and cover relations $x_1>x_2>x_3$, $x_2<x_4$ and $x_4>x_5$, for $i\ge 3$, $x_{2i-1}< x_{2i}$ and $x_{2i}> x_{2i+1}$.
head: environment

label: lem:conexp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:conexp}

The filter lattice $\mathcal{F}(P)$ is considered as a convex expansion, that is for every $x\in P$,
	\[
	\mathcal{F}(P)\cong \mathcal{F}(P-x)\boxplus \mathcal{F}(P*x),
	\]
  where $P-x$ and $P*x$ the induced subposets on $P\setminus\{x\}$ and $P\setminus\{y \in P|y \leq x \text{ or } x \leq y\}$, respectively.
head: environment

label: lem:struc
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:struc}
  Let $\Phi_n$ be the $n$-th FLC defined above. Then
  \[
\Phi_n \cong \Gamma_{n-1}^* \boxplus \Gamma_{n-4}^* \cong \left((\Gamma_{n-3}^* \boxplus \Gamma_{n-3}^*) \boxplus \Gamma_{n-4}^*\right) \boxplus \Gamma_{n-4}^* \; (n\ge 5).
\]
or 
  \[
  \Phi_n \cong \Phi_{n-1} \boxplus \Phi_{n-2} \cong (\Phi_{n-2} \boxplus \Phi_{n-2}) \boxplus \Phi_{n-3} \; (n\ge 6).
  \]
head: environment

title: Proof.
body_md: By definition of $\Phi_n$, the result is easily obtained by putting $x=x_n$ and $x=x_3$ in Lemma \ref{lem:conexp}, respectively.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: The number of vertices of $\Phi_n$ is $2F_n$.

label: prop:rec-AB
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof.
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:rec-R},   for $m\ge 4$,
    \begin{align*}
    A_m(x) &=B_{m-1}(x)+x^2A_{m-1}(x)\\
    &=xA_{m-1}(x)+B_{m-2}(x)+x^2A_{m-1}(x)\\
    &=xA_{m-1}(x)+A_{m-1}(x)-x^2A_{m-2}(x)+x^2A_{m-1}(x)\\
    &=(1+x+x^2)A_{m-1}(x)-x^2A_{m-2}(x).
    \end{align*}
                 
                
                                  
                                                
                                                           
                                          
              
	For $B_2(x)$, the conclusion is also ture.
Samilarily, the recurrence relation of $B_m(x)$ can be obtained.
head: environment

label: th:gf-AB
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:gf-AB}
	The generating functions of $A_m(x)$ and $B_m(x)$ are
	\[
	\sum_{m\ge 0}A_m(x)z^m = z+ \frac{1-z+z^2}{1-(1+x+x^2)z+x^2z^2}
	\]
	and
	\[
	\sum_{m\ge0}B_m(x)z^m = \frac{1+x-(x+x^2)z}{1-(1+x+x^2)z+x^2z^2},
	\]
	respectively.
head: environment

title: Proof.
body_md:
By the Proposition~\ref{prop:rec-AB},
	\begin{align*}
	\sum_{m\ge 0}A_m(x)z^m &= \sum_{m\ge 4}A_m(x)z^m +A_3(x)z^3 + A_2(x)z^2 + A_1(x)y+A_0(x) \\
	  &= \sum_{m\ge 4}((1+x+x^2)A_{m-1}-x^2A_{m-2})z^m +A_3(x)z^3 + A_2(x)z^2 + A_1(x)z+A_0(x) \\
	  &= (1+x+x^2)z\sum_{m\ge 3} A_m(x)z^m - x^2z^2 \sum_{m\ge 2} A_m(x)z^m A_3(x)z^3+ A_2(x)z^2 + A_1(x)z+A_0(x) \\
	  &= (1+x+x^2)z\sum_{m\ge 0} A_m(x)z^m - x^2z^2 \sum_{m\ge 0} A_m(x)z^m + 1 +x^2z^3-xz^2-x^2z^2.
    \end{align*}
Similarly, the generating function of $B_m$ are obtained.
head: environment

label: th:rnk
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof.
body_md:
Consider the polynomials $g_n(x)$ defined by
     \[
     \sum_{n\ge 0}g_n(x)z^n =\frac{1}{1-(1+x+x^2)z+x^2z^2}
     \]
     such that
     \[
     g_n(x) =\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(-1)^i \binom{n-i}{i}x^{2i}(1+x+x^2)^{n-2i}.
     \]
     In addition, the coefficient of $x^k$ in $g_n(x)$ can be given by
     \[
     [x^k]g_n(x) =\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(-1)^i\binom{n-i}{i}x^{2i}(1+x+x^2)^{n-2i} =\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(-1)^i\binom{n-i}{i}\binom{n-2i;3}{k-2i}.
     \]
     Then, since $A_m(x)=z +g_m(x)-g_{m-1}(x) +g_{m-2}(x)$, we have
     \begin{align*}
       r_{2m,k} &= [x^k]A_m(x)=[x^k]z +[x^k]g_m(x)-[x^k]g_{m-1}(x) +[x^k]g_{m-2}(x)\\
                &= \delta_{1,m}\delta_{0,k}+ \sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor \frac m2 \rfloor}(-1)^i\binom{m-i}{i} \binom{m-2i;3}{k-2i} -\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor \frac{m-1}{2} \rfloor}(-1)^i\binom{m-i-1}{i}\binom{m-2i-1;3}{k-2i}\\
                 &~+\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor \frac{m-2}{2} \rfloor}(-1)^i\binom{m-i-2}{i}\binom{m-2i-2;3}{k-2i}.
     \end{align*}
     Thus, $r_{2m+1,k}$ is obtained from $B_m(x)=g_m(x)+xg_m(x)-xg_{m-1}(x)-x^2g_{m-1}(x)$ in the same way.
head: environment

label: th:rnx
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:rnx}
	The generating function of $R_n(x)$ is
	\[
	\sum_{n\ge 0}R_n(x)y^n = \frac{1+(1+x)y-(x+x^2)y^3-(x +x^2)y^4+x^2y^6}{1-(1+x+x^2)y^2+x^2y^4}.
	\]
head: environment

title: Proof.
body_md:
By the definition of $A_m(x)$ and $B_m(x)$,
	\begin{align*}
	\sum_{n\ge0}R_n(x)y^n &= \sum_{m\ge 0}A_m(x)y^{2m} + \sum_{m\ge 0}B_m(x)y^{2m+1} \\
	&= \sum_{m\ge 0}A_m(x)y^{2m} + y\sum_{m\ge 0}B_m(x)y^{2m} \\
	&= \frac{1-xy^4-x^2y^4+x^2y^6}{1-(1+x+x^2)y^2+x^2y^4} + y\frac{1+x-xy^2-x^2y^2}{1-(1+x+x^2)y^2+x^2y^4} \\
	&= \frac{1+(1+x)y-(x+x^2)y^3-(x +x^2)y^4+x^2y^6} {1-(1+x+x^2)y^2+x^2y^4}.
	\end{align*}
head: environment

label: cor:fibs
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:fibs} Using the above notation, we have 
  	$$  \sum_{k=0}^{n} r_{n,k} = 2F_n \;\; (n \geq 3).  $$

label: lem:enum
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:enum}
  Let $L$ be a finite distributive lattice and $K$ a cutting of $L$. Then
  \[
  q_k(L\boxplus K) = q_k(L) + q_k(K) + q_{k-1}(K).
  \]

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:rec-q}
  For $n\ge 4$,
  \[
  q_{n,k} = q_{n-1,k}+q_{n-2,k}+q_{n-2,k-1}.
  \]

	For $n\ge 5$,
	\[
	Q_n(x) = Q_{n-1}(x) + (1+x)Q_{n-2}(x).
	\]

title: Proof.

label: th:gf-Q
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:gf-Q}
  The generating function of $Q_n(x)$ is
  \[
  \sum_{n\ge 0}Q_n(x)y^n =\frac{1+(1+x)y-(1+x)^2y^3-(1+x)^2y^4}{1-y-(1+x)y^2}.
  \]
head: environment

label: prop:RF-q
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:RF-q}
	For $n \ge 0$,
	\[
	Q_n(x)=\sum_{j= 0}^{\lfloor \frac{n+1}{2} \rfloor}\binom{n-j+1}{j}(1+x)^j -
 \sum_{j= 2}^{\lfloor \frac{n+1}{2} \rfloor}\binom{n-j-1}{j-2}(1+x)^j - \sum_{j= 2}^{\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor}\binom{n-j-2}{j-2}(1+x)^j.
	\]
	and thus
	\[
	q_{n,k}=\sum_{j= 0}^{\lfloor \frac{n+1}{2} \rfloor}\binom{n-j+1}{j}\binom jk -
 \sum_{j= 2}^{\lfloor \frac{n+1}{2} \rfloor}\binom{n-j-1}{j-2}\binom jk - \sum_{j= 2}^{\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor}\binom{n-j-2}{j-2}\binom jk.
	\]
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
For $n\ge 3$, the number of vertices of $\Phi_n$ is
     \[
     q_{n,0}= 2\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \rfloor} \binom{n-1-k}{k} = 2F_n.
     \]

label: th:gf-D
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:gf-D}
  The generating function of $D_n(x)$ is given by
  \[
  \sum_{n\ge 0}D_n(x)y^n = -y+xy+x^2y^2+\frac{1+y -x^2y^2} {(1-xy)(1-xy^2)-xy^3}.
  \]

label: pro:d
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro:d}
  For $n\ge 3$, the number of vertices of degree $k$ of $\Phi_n$ is
  \[
  d_{n,k} = \sum_{j=0}^k\left(\binom{n-2j}{k-j}\binom{j}{n-k-j} +\binom{n-2j-1}{k-j}\binom{j}{n-k-j-1} -\binom{n-2j-2}{k-j-2}\binom{j}{n-k-j}\right).
  \]
head: environment

title: Proof.
body_md:
The way is similar to the method of \cite{aKlavzMP11}. Using the expansion

\[
\frac{x^n}{(1-x)^{n+1}} =\sum_{j\ge n}\binom{j}{n}x^j,
\]

we consider the formal power series expansion of
 \[
 f(x,y) =\frac{1}{(1-xy)(1-xy^2)-xy^3},
 \]
 \begin{align*}
     f(x,y) &= \frac{1}{(1-xy)(1-xy^2)-xy^3}\\
       &= \frac{(1-xy)^{-1}(1-xy^2)^{-1}}{1-xy^3(1-xy)^{-1}(1-xy^2)^{-1}}\\
       &= \sum_{t \ge 0 }x^t y^{3t}(1-xy)^{-t-1}(1-xy^2)^{-t-1}\\
       &= \sum_{t \ge 0} \frac{(xy)^t}{(1-xy)^{t+1}} \frac{(xy^2)^t}{(1-xy^2)^{t+1}}x^{-t}\\
       &= \sum_{t\ge 0} \sum_{i\ge t} \binom it (xy)^i \sum_{j\ge t}\binom jt (xy^2)^j x^{-t}\\
       &= \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{k=0}^n \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{n-2j}{k-j} \binom{j}{n-k-j}x^ky^n.
 \end{align*}

Thus
 \[
 [x^k][y^n]f(x,y) =\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{n-2j}{k-j} \binom{j}{n-k-j}.
 \]
 Note that
 $$
 \frac{1+y-x^2y^2}{(1-xy)(1-xy^2)-xy^3} =f(x,y) +yf(x,y)-x^2y^2f(x,y),
 $$
 then
 \begin{align*}
   &~[x^k][y^n]\frac{1+y-x^2y^2}{(1-xy)(1-xy^2)-xy^3}\\
   &= [x^k][y^n]f(x,y) +[x^k][y^{n-1}]f(x,y) -[x^{k-2}][y^{n-2}]f(x,y)\\
   &= \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{n-2j}{k-j}\binom{j}{n-k-j} +\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{n-2j-1}{k-j}\binom{j}{n-k-j-1}\\ &~-\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{n-2j-2}{k-j-2}\binom{j}{n-k-j}.
 \end{align*}
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
For $n \geq 3$,
  	$$\sum_{k=0}^n d_{n,k}=2F_n.$$

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro:out-d}
For $n \ge 3$ and $k \ge 1$,
	\[
	d_{n,k}^- = d_{n-1,k}^- + d_{n-2,k-1}^-.
	\]

label: pro:ouD
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro:ouD}
	For $n \ge 5$,
	\[
	D_n^-(x) = D_{n-1}^-(x) + xD_{n-2}^-(x).
	\]
head: environment

label: prop:QD-
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{prop:QD-}
	For $n \ge 0$,
	\[
	D_n^-(1+x) = Q_n(x).
	\]
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
The generating function of $D_n^-(x)$ is
	\[
	\sum_{n\ge 0} D_n^-(x)y^n = \frac{1+xy-x^2y^3-x^2y^4}{1-y-xy^2}.
	\]
head: environment

label: pro:ou-d
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro:ou-d}
	For $n \ge 0$,
	\[
	D_n^-(x) =\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor} \left( \binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-k}{k}\right)x^k.
	\]
	Thus
	\[
	d_{n,k}^- =  \binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-k}{k}.
	\]
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
For $n \geq 3$,
	$$\sum_{k=0}^n d_{n,k}^- = \sum_{k=0}^n \left( \binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-k}{k} \right) = 2F_n.$$
